notes: Page 2 shows two minifigure builds (helmet, visor, head, torso, legs, backpack) whose parts are not in the set's parts list, so they are not recorded as pieces.

The only listed pieces on this page are the Space Gun (b1, lego-4360) and the Trans-Red 1x1 cone (b2) pushed onto its muzzle. The cone is a side attachment, not stacked on the gun, so it is recorded as a joined edge. The gun's catalogue ports are only clip.1, so the gun side of that edge has no port.
The alien minifigure holding the gun is not in the parts list and is not recorded.
Step 1: Black Plate 2 x 6 (b3), the model's first piece, so it rests on nothing.

Step 2: White inverted slope brick (b4) is identified as lego-4854, the only white inverted slope in the parts list. It sits on the plate b3 and covers four of the six stud columns, leaving the 2x2 at the left end exposed. The joined edge stands in for rests_on [b3].
Page 3 also shows a picture of the finished model, which adds no pieces.

Step 3: The white curved inverted 6x4 wedge (b5, lego-43713) is shown only in the parts callout and already in place in the drawing. I took it to sit over the black plate b3 and the white slope b4, and listed both as supports. The dark gray inverted 3x2 slope (b6) is then pressed onto the rear studs of b5.

Step 4: Two black 1x6 plates (b7, b8) go along the two sides of the hull on b5. I assumed their rear ends also overlap the studs of b6, so both list b6 as a support. This is hard to confirm from the drawing.
The schema has no rests_on field, so each resting relationship is recorded as a joined edge with method 'stud'.

Step 5: The black 4x4 plate (b9) goes on the front of the hull over b5, b7 and b8. The two white 4x2 wedge bricks go on the rear. One is already in place in the drawing and the other is being lowered, so I recorded both. Which wedge is which side is not certain; I took the left wedge (b10, lego-41768) as the far side on b7 and the right wedge (b11, lego-41767) as the near side on b8. Both are assumed to also touch the studs of the gray slope b6.

Step 6: The callout shows a white 1x4 brick, two 1x4 panels (lego-43337) and the blue lever (lego-298c02). The drawing does not show clearly how the 1x4 brick and panels stack. I assumed the brick (b12) sits on the near plate b8 with panel b14 on top, and panel b13 sits on the far plate b7. The lever (b15) sits on the 4x4 plate b9.
The schema has no rests_on field, so each resting relationship is recorded as a joined edge with method 'stud'.

Step 7: A small sub-assembly is built first. The long blue pin (b19) goes through the gray Technic 1x1 (b18) and into the white Technic 1x2 (b16). A short black pin (b17) goes into the other hole of the 1x2. The sub-assembly is then placed on the black 4x4 plate b9 at the stern.
Both b16 and b18 sit on b9, recorded as joined edges with method 'stud' since the schema has no rests_on field. Exact stud positions on b9 are not clear from the drawing.
Pin joints are recorded as 'revolute' insert joints. The pins have friction, so they could be treated as rigid instead.

The page shows steps 9 and 10. Step 8 is not on this page and the printed page 7 was skipped, so anything added in step 8 is not recorded. Step 9's drawing already shows a gray piece at the stern that I cannot account for from this page.

Step 9: The light gray hinge base (b20) and two clip plates (b21, b22) go on the rear of the black 4x4 plate b9. I could not see which studs they use, so b9 is recorded as the only support. They may also clutch pieces from step 8.

Step 10: Two sub-assemblies are built, each with a trans-green 1x1 round plate pushed onto the end of a white gun/torch (lego-3959). Each gun then clips into one of the clip plates. Which gun goes into which clip is arbitrary.
The schema has no rests_on field, so each resting relationship is recorded as a joined edge with method 'stud'.

This is printed page 7, which came after the step 9-10 page in the sequence. Step 8 repeats step 7 on the other side of the stern: a long blue pin joins a gray Technic 1x1 to a white Technic 1x2, a short black pin goes in the 1x2's other hole, and the sub-assembly goes on the black 4x4 plate b9. This explains the second Technic assembly seen at the stern in step 9.
The two new bricks (b27, b29) sit on b9 beside the step 7 pair. I recorded b9 as their only support because the exact stud positions are not clear from the drawing.
The schema has no rests_on field, so each resting relationship is recorded as a joined edge with method 'stud'.

Step 11: A white 1x2 tile (b31) and a black 2x2 hinge top plate (b32) are added. The tile is shown only in the callout and already in place in the drawing. I took it to sit on the two light gray Technic 1x1 bricks (b18, b29) side by side. This is a guess from the drawing.
The black hinge plate b32 is lowered onto the stern hinge base b20, so it is recorded as a hinge join. I did not add stud contacts for it.
The schema has no rests_on field, so resting is recorded as a joined edge with method 'stud'.

Step 12: Two white Technic panel fairings (the wings) are pushed onto the pins that stick out of the stern Technic assemblies. One wing is drawn already in place and the other is being added. The wing with the three visible pin holes is recorded as the far-side one (b33, lego-64681) and the other as the near-side one (b34, lego-64393). Which part number goes on which side is a guess from the drawing.
I assumed the far wing goes onto the b27 pins (b28 black, b30 blue) and the near wing onto the b16 pins (b17 black, b19 blue). Each wing uses two of its pin holes.
A sticker from the sheet (b35) is applied to the white 1x2 tile b31 (the arrow points to it). The sticker is recorded as one part joined to the tile.
No other parts are added on this page.

Step 13: Two bar-pin pieces are taken as lego-61184 (the parts list has 2x of them) and get a light cover on the bar: Trans-Red (b38) on b36, Trans-Dark Blue (b39) on b37. The blue light looks lighter in the drawing, but the parts list only has Trans-Dark Blue for this piece.
The red-light pin goes in the far wing (b33) and the blue-light pin in the near wing (b34). The exact pin hole used is a guess; I picked pin-hole.3 on each wing.
Two 'POLICE' stickers are applied, one on each wing. They come from the single sticker sheet b35, so I added joined edges from b35 to b33 and b34 with no new part.
The sticker edges use method 'sticker' and reversible 'damaging'.

Step 14: The black bracket (b40) is shown only in the callout and already in place in the drawing, with its flat part on the rear studs of the two white 4x2 wedge bricks (b10, b11) and its vertical face at the tail end. The cone (b41) is pushed onto the studs on that vertical face, turned sideways, as the arrows show.
I assumed the bracket sits on both wedge bricks, one stud row on each. The exact studs are a guess from the drawing.
The schema has no rests_on field, so resting is recorded as a joined edge with method 'stud'.

Step 15: The callout shows the Right (b42, lego-54383) and Left (b43, lego-54384) 6x3 wedge plates. The drawing shows them already together as one swept wing across the top of the hull, and I could not see the joint between them.
I assumed they lie over the white curved brick b5 and the two angled wedge bricks, with the right plate on b11 and the left plate on b10. The exact support pieces are uncertain.
The schema has no rests_on field, so resting is recorded as a joined edge with method 'stud'.

Step 16: The black 1x4 plate (b44) is laid along the middle of the wing, across the joint between the two wedge plates b42 and b43. The white tail fin (b45, lego-44661) sits on the studs of the black bracket b40 at the tail end.
Which stud positions on b40 the fin uses is a guess from the drawing.
The schema has no rests_on field, so resting is recorded as a joined edge with method 'stud'.

Step 17: The black 3x4 wedge plate (b50) goes over the black 1x4 plate b44 and the two wing wedges b42 and b43. The clip tiles (b46, b47) and the Trans-Dark Blue and Trans-Red tiles (b49, b48) go on the wing tips. The drawing already shows all of them in place.

I assumed the Trans-Dark Blue tile and one clip tile are on the left wing wedge b43, and the Trans-Red tile and the other clip tile are on the right wing wedge b42. The side assignment is a guess from the drawing, as is the exact stud use.
A sticker from the sheet (b35) goes on the tail fin b45, per the arrow. It is recorded as a joined edge to the existing sticker sheet part.
The schema has no rests_on field, so resting is recorded as a joined edge with method 'stud'.
Step 18: The white 4x4 triple wedged slope (b51, lego-48933) is shown in the callout and already in place in the drawing. It sits on the black 3x4 wedge plate b50, the part most clearly under it.
It may also touch the neighbouring wing wedges or the 1x4 plate b44 below. That cannot be told from the drawing, so I recorded b50 only.
The schema has no rests_on field, so resting is recorded as a joined edge with method 'stud'.

Step 19: Two black Technic pin connectors with bar (b52, b53) are clipped into the clip tiles at the two wing tips. Their bars snap into the clips, and I recorded them as free to rotate. The drawing already shows them in place.

A Trans-Red cheese slope (b54) and a Trans-Dark Blue cheese slope (b55) go side by side on the studs at the front of the white 4x4 wedged slope b51. I picked stud.1.1 and stud.1.2 on b51, but the exact studs are a guess from the drawing.
The schema has no rests_on field, so resting is recorded as a joined edge with method 'stud'.

Step 20: The step is built twice. In each copy a Trans-Green 1x1 cone is pushed onto the end of a light gray Technic pin (lego-4274), the only 2x pin of that type in the parts list. Each pin then goes into one hole of a black pin connector (b52, b53) at the wing tips, shooting forward.
I picked pin-hole.1 on each connector and arbitrarily paired b56 with b53 and b57 with b52. The page also carries a warning symbol (do not fire the pieces at faces), which adds nothing to the build.
The pin and cone pieces are listed as separate parts, one entry per physical piece.
Step 21: The Trans-Dark Blue windscreen (b60) closes the cockpit. The drawing shows it already in place, covering the open area between the stern and the wedge bricks.
I assumed it clutches the two side panels (b13, b14), the sticker tile (b31) and the white curved brick b5. The exact studs it uses are a guess from the drawing.
The page also shows the finished model with the two minifigures, which are not in the parts list and are not recorded.
The schema has no rests_on field, so resting is recorded as a joined edge with method 'stud'.
This page is the parts inventory with element numbers and has no building step, so it adds no pieces or joins.

Correction to earlier pages: this page shows element 4520320 (2x) as the long gray pin used in step 20, which is lego-61184. The short gray pin with a bar head that carries the red and blue lights in step 13 is element 4550643, which matches the parts list's lego-4274 (Technic Pin 1/2) better. So the step 13 pins (b36, b37) should be lego-4274 and the step 20 pins (b56, b57) should be lego-61184. I swapped these before seeing the inventory. The pin counts are unchanged and the joins still hold, but the two type ids are exchanged.

The two groups are the Raid VPR ship (b3 to b60) and the Space Gun with its Trans-Red cone (b1, b2) from page 2. I am keeping them separate because the booklet builds the gun as a minifigure accessory: the alien holds it, and no step attaches it to the ship. Its only join is the cone on the gun, which is already recorded.

I did not add a made-up edge from the gun to the ship. The ship's clips hold the wing-tip pin connectors, not the gun, and the booklet never shows the gun clipped to the ship. The minifigures are not in the parts list, so they are not nodes that could join the two groups.

Still open from earlier pages: element numbers on the parts-inventory page indicate the step 13 pins (b36, b37) are lego-4274 and the step 20 pins (b56, b57) are lego-61184. I typed them the other way round and cannot change an existing piece here, so the two type ids are exchanged. The joins are unaffected.

I am keeping the two groups separate. The group of two is the Space Gun with its Trans-Red cone (b1, b2) from page 2. The booklet never attaches it to the ship; it is shown only in the alien minifigure's hand, and the minifigures are not in the parts list.
Adding any edge between the gun and the ship would invent a connection the booklet does not show, so I left the graph unchanged. The remaining 58 pieces (b3 to b60) form one connected model.
The note about the swapped 4274 and 61184 type ids on the step 13 and step 20 pins (b36, b37 and b56, b57) still applies. It does not affect connectivity.
